title: A Predictive SaaS System Based on GRU and XGBoost Models to Increase User Conversion Rates in Technological Retail E-Commerce Platforms
content: E-commerce platforms in the technological retail sector face persistent challenges in transforming digital browsing traffic into completed sales due to high shopping cart and session abandonment rates (averaging 78.5% in emerging Latin American markets). While previous studies address online purchase intention through isolated static classifiers or offline sequential recommenders, few solutions integrate real-time sequential-tabular inference with immediate commercial intervention within a scalable cloud architecture. This article presents the design, cloud implementation, and empirical validation of a predictive Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) system powered by a hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) engine to increase user conversion rates on technological retail e-commerce platforms in Lima, Peru. The methodology encompasses real-time clickstream telemetry capture, hybrid session representation combining 64-unit GRU temporal embeddings with aggregated session attributes, synthetic minority over-sampling (SMOTE) on training partitions, TreeSHAP interpretability, and deployment on an Amazon Web Services (AWS) microservices architecture featuring dual persistence in Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL). Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the hybrid GRU + XGBoost model achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.937 and an F1-Score of 0.930, outperforming standalone sequential and tabular baselines while maintaining an average end-to-end inference latency of 0.43 s (430 ms) and a streaming ingestion latency of 40 ms. Furthermore, a dual-front expert validation protocol yielded mean scores of 4.60/5.00 in the technical domain and 4.50/5.00 in the technological retail business domain, confirming the system’s mathematical robustness, low-latency scalability, and commercial viability for real-time abandonment mitigation.
